verifications.claim: Immunization prevents millions of deaths annually.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'vaccines have aided humanity in preventing many infectious diseases... saved countless lives'; R4: 'Vaccines help protect millions of healthy people'; R11: 'immunization currently saves an estimated 3 million lives per year worldwide'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state vaccines/immunization save millions or 3 million lives annually.

verifications.claim: Vaccines introduce deactivated or weakened parts of a virus or bacteria (antigens) into the body.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'germs in the vaccine have been killed or weakened... Some vaccines contain only a part of the germ'; R5: 'weakened (attenuated) form... Killed (inactivated) vaccines are made from a protein or other small pieces'
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches descriptions of killed/weakened germs or parts (antigens).

verifications.claim: Vaccines cause an imitation infection that does not cause disease.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'your body is tricked into thinking that it has been infected... without getting the disease'; R5: 'Vaccines imitate an infection... without the risk of a full-blown infection'; R15: 'trigger an immune response without causing illness'
verifications.reasoning: Exact phrasing of imitation/tricked infection without disease.

verifications.claim: Vaccines teach the immune system to create T-lymphocytes and B-lymphocytes (memory cells).
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'development of memory cells'; R2: 'makes antibodies... remember how to fight the germ'
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention memory cells and antibodies (B cells), but do not explicitly name T- and B-lymphocytes as created by vaccines.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'memory cells that can recognize and fight pathogens if they reoccur'; R2: 'antibodies... remember how to fight the germ'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states memory cells/antibodies remember pathogens.

verifications.claim: Memory cells allow for a rapid response upon future exposure.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'If the germs from the disease enter your body in the future, the antibodies destroy the germs before you can become sick'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly describes rapid destruction before illness on re-exposure.

verifications.claim: Active immunization teaches the body to produce its own antibodies.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R15: 'Active Immunization: ... The body produces its own antibodies'; R16: 'active immunization... producing substances (such as antibodies)'
verifications.reasoning: Precisely matches definition of active immunization.

verifications.claim: Types of active immunization include inactivated vaccines, live-attenuated vaccines, messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines, and subunit/conjugate vaccines.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'mRNA vaccines, subunit, recombinant, or conjugate vaccines, live attenuated vaccines, and inactivated or dead vaccines'; R4: 'live-attenuated vaccine, inactivated vaccine, subunit, recombinant, polysaccharide, and conjugate vaccine'; R5: lists mRNA, inactivated, live attenuated
verifications.reasoning: All listed types explicitly mentioned as vaccine types.

verifications.claim: Passive immunization provides temporary protection by introducing antibodies directly (e.g., immunoglobulin) from another human or animal source.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R15: 'Passive Immunization: ... introducing antibodies directly (e.g., immunoglobulin) from another human or animal source... temporary'; R16: 'Passive immunization... antibodies... from animals (usually horses)... pooled human immune globulin'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match including example and temporary nature.

verifications.claim: Routine pediatric vaccinations include DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), MMR (measles, mumps, rubella), Varicella (chickenpox), Hib, Pneumococcal, and Polio.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough [pertussis], Haemophilus influenzae type b [Hib], pneumococcal disease, polio, measles, mumps, rubella, ... chickenpox'; R8: lists DTaP, MMR, Varicella, Hib, Pneumococcal, Polio
verifications.reasoning: All vaccines listed as routine pediatric ones.

verifications.claim: Adolescents and adults vaccinations include HPV (human papillomavirus), COVID-19, Influenza, and Tdap.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'human papillomavirus'; R10: 'COVID-19 vaccine Flu vaccine (influenza) Tdap vaccine'
verifications.reasoning: Directly lists these as recommended for adolescents/adults.

verifications.claim: Common vaccine side effects include fever, pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R17: 'Common reactions include pain, redness, and swelling... mild and limited in duration'
verifications.reasoning: Exactly matches common local side effects.

verifications.claim: Serious side effects of vaccines are rare.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R11: 'serious vaccine side effects are very rare'
